key_correction: I had assumed GraphicsEngine::Initialize would precede CreateDevice. The call order in Engine::Initialize is the reverse: the device is created first, then the graphics resources are initialised.

call_order.0x18007476b: GraphicsEngine::GraphicsEngine() at 0x90730, on a 0x1C0-byte allocation stored to Engine+0x1F8
call_order.0x180074781: GraphicsEngine::CreateDevice(EWindow*, GraphicsEngineSettings const&) at 0x90ba0, with rdx = window, r8 = settings
call_order.0x180074aca: GraphicsEngine::Initialize(EWindow*, settings const&, ResourceLoader*) at 0x90e60, with rdx = window, r8 = settings, r9 = [Engine+0x210]

argument_map_for_engine_initialize.rdx: EWindow* (kept in r15), passed through to CreateDevice and GraphicsEngine::Initialize
argument_map_for_engine_initialize.r8: GraphicsEngineSettings const* (kept in r12), passed through likewise
argument_map_for_engine_initialize.stack+0xA0: FileSystem*, stored to [this+0x358] and never read or dereferenced anywhere in Initialize

filesystem_may_be_null: The FileSystem pointer is stored once at [this+0x358] and is never loaded again inside the 3049-byte body, so passing null does not fault there. Whether a later subsystem dereferences it out of band is not established.
resource_loader_is_internal: ResourceLoader is created inside Initialize and stored at [this+0x210] at 0x1800748f5, then reused at five later sites. A host does not need to build or supply it.
graphics_engine_initialize_nature: Its body contains no CreateDevice call. It performs six repeated rounds of allocation, string construction, a call to 0x1972c0 and one to 0x23090, which reads as populating internal resource or shader tables rather than creating the device.
not_established: the meaning of the four trailing strings and the five booleans
whether the six rounds in GraphicsEngine::Initialize depend on files being present
whether any later engine subsystem dereferences the FileSystem pointer
